title: A Case of the Mondays: Do Not Disturb
summary: Commanders 27, Eagles 10: a 10-0 hole, a referee swap nobody told me about, 27 unanswered points, Antonio Williams doing Terry's celebration, my first good pick of the season, and a group chat that thought I was asleep.
paragraphs: I called it. Commanders 27, Eagles 13. Final score: Commanders 27, Eagles 10. I nailed our number to the point and missed theirs by three, and according to my own group chat, I slept through the whole thing.

On Friday I told you I'd be on my couch "fighting to stay awake past midnight like the 45-year-old I am." My last message to the chat went out at 9:28 p.m. After that, silence. At 11:14, Chris announced to the room: "Ben's gonna be so surprised when he wakes up." Chris, I was awake. I was awake for every snap. I put my phone on Do Not Disturb so that if I did fall asleep, you two couldn't spoil it for me. I'd like to thank both of you for your concern, and for confirming that the plan worked perfectly.
## The Undercard

UVA spent Halloween in Winston-Salem and lost to No. 14 Wake Forest, 51-7. Fifty-one to seven. Wake scored on its first nine possessions, which I didn't know was allowed, and we went 1-for-12 on third down. It was bad. So bad. And it was a road game, so I didn't even have the President's Box buffet to eat my feelings into.

That's three straight losses and a 4-5 record, one year after the best season this program has had in a long time. Here's the bright side: a UVA loss has never once ruined my Sunday, and this one had the decency to wrap up Saturday evening, which left a full day to recover. As it turns out, that was the correct order of operations. Get your heartbreak out of the way early, then go win on Sunday night.
## The First Quarter

Let's start at the beginning, because the first fifteen minutes went exactly the way a 1-4-1 team's first fifteen minutes should. Luke McCaffrey opened the night with a 44-yard kickoff return to midfield, and we celebrated that by committing back-to-back false starts and missing a field goal. Then Chig Okonkwo got stripped at our own 10, and Saquon Barkley walked it in from three yards out. Eagles 10, Commanders 0.

The group chat handled it with its usual grace. Jason: "We're a bad football team." Then: "Poorly coached." Chris: "This team should be going for it on like every single 4th down. It's our only chance." I said "God this is gross," then "I haaaate Collinsworth," and then, in the same minute, "He's not wrong," which is the most honest pair of sentences ever typed about Cris Collinsworth.

Jayden felt the same way, just with a podium. "Honestly, it was complete B.S.," he said after the game, and he said something to the team about it during the game. Whatever it was, I'd like it printed and laminated.
## Ref Watch: The Ref Who Wasn't There

I spent all of last week warning you about Alex Moore. I put him in the Hail Mail. I put him in the post. I built a whole [Ref Watch page](whos-reffing.html) so you could see exactly how many flags his crews throw. At 9:27 Sunday night, I typed "This ref throws the most flags in the NFL" into the group chat with total confidence.

It was not Alex Moore. The NFL pulled his crew off our game after a rough night at Packers-Lions the week before, sent him to Patriots-Dolphins, and handed us Shawn Hochuli instead. Yes, that Shawn Hochuli, from the NFC Championship. The guy who stood at the goal line in Philadelphia and explained he could just award the Eagles a touchdown if we kept it up. Nobody told me. I yelled at the wrong man for an entire quarter.

Chris, meanwhile, came out of nowhere with the worst take of the season: "I get he throws a lot of flags but these seem legitimate to me? We could, you know, not false start?" I wrote back, "Chris… no. That's too obvious." I stand by it. Accountability is for teams with winning records.

For the record, I thought there were a ton of weak flags. Final count: 15 flags, nine on us for 70 yards and six on them for 30. That's a little above Hochuli's 14.5 a game, and still under the 16.8 Moore's crews average, so the league's switch technically spared us. Hochuli has now had us twice this year. We lost in Dallas and won Sunday, so he's 1-1, the most average possible result. One roughing call was "pretty weak," per JP Finlay, and then the Eagles answered with a false start, an illegal formation and a doinked short field goal, which Finlay called the football gods making up for it. I'm not going to argue with the football gods. They've been a little cold to us lately. Weak flags and all, we won. I'll allow it.
## 27 Unanswered

Then the Commanders scored the next 27 points, and the Eagles didn't score again all night. Jayden hit Treylon Burks deep. Ben Standig noted that Burks "has been huge since that early third-down drop," which is the nicest possible way to say a man made up for something. Chig Okonkwo, two quarters after the fumble, made a rotating one-handed catch that belongs on a cereal box. Drew Stevens kicked field goal after field goal. Rachaad White ripped off 33 yards to get inside the 5, then put the exclamation point on it.

And Antonio Williams played 83 percent of the snaps, made an incredible grab on a strike from Jayden, and celebrated with Terry's Scary Terry move. Back in August I said the rookie had some McLaurin to his game, with every caveat a man can attach to a preseason opinion. Dan Quinn said Sunday, "the moment is never too big for him." The receivers all said they wanted to play well for Terry. Jayden said they wanted to "show love to him to (let him) know he's always on our mind." That's the second-best part of the whole night.

The defense might have been the best part. Tanner McKee got sacked four times and hit nine. Dorance Armstrong knocked the ball loose and Charles Omenihu fell on it. Nick Cross stuffed a third down, the sub couldn't stop talking about Trey Amos, and Rasul Douglas ended it with an interception. Philadelphia went 5-for-15 on third down and was shut out for the last three quarters. Yes, it was Tanner McKee. Somebody on r/Commanders put it best: "We beat the practice squad. Simmer down." No. I've been simmered down since September 27. I'm boiling now.

It was Jayden's first win as a starter since October 5, 2025. Asked about the wait, he said, "It probably felt longer." Here's the part that broke my brain: according to Standig, that win, at the Chargers, was also 27-10, and also came by scoring the final 27 points. This team only knows how to win one way, and it's this one. Jayden also got the wind knocked out of him on a hard hit late in the first half and stayed in the game. My heart dropped into my socks. The group chat, of course, never heard about it, because I was on Do Not Disturb, panicking alone like a professional.
Quinn summed it up the way only a coach with a 2-4-1 record can: "Tonight, we got three (quarters). We need all four." Dan, I'll take three. Three is a lot more than we've been getting.
## The Group Chat

By the fourth quarter, the chat had gone from despair to suspicious optimism, which is the most Commanders emotion there is. Jason, at 11:07: "Welp. Prob gonna sneak out a win. Season is alive for at least another 12 days." Then, before bed, the line I want to end every season on: "A win is a win. They're too rare and life's too short so gonna enjoy it."
And Chris's hypothetical baby, the one conceived the night we beat Seattle, can finally stop crawling. I still don't think that's how babies work.
## Call Your Shot

Eighty-three percent of you had us winning, and the crowd's median pick was 26-14, which honestly might be better than mine overall. CryoGen called 31-17, right winner, off by 11. But the closest named call on the board, for the first time all season, was me: 27-13, off by three.

Which means that after starting the year 0-2, I am now in first place on the season leaderboard at 1-2, off by 6.7 a game, just ahead of Taylor P (1-0, off by 7) and CryoGen (1-0, off by 11). Taylor, it was nice while it lasted. And if the Eagles make that short field goal, I hit the score exactly. I have never been this upset about a doink in my life. [The Rams are next](leaderboard.html), and the poll's already open. Come take this away from me.
## Roll Call

A quick update for our reader from DC, whose game-day ritual is to rotate outfits until we win, then wear that exact combination until we lose. My friend, you've been rotating since September 27. Sunday night, an outfit finally got promoted. Wear it Sunday. Maybe wash it first. Actually, no. Don't risk it.
## Next Up

So: 2-4-1, the Rams at home Sunday at 1, and a trade deadline on November 10. Pro Football Talk reports we're one of three teams interested in Jacksonville receiver Brian Thomas Jr., which I'll believe when I see him in burgundy, and then I'll believe it a lot. Win Sunday and everyone goes back to pretending we're buyers.
Kickoff's at 1 p.m. this week. No 8:20, no midnight, and I'll be off Do Not Disturb. Chris, Jason: you're allowed to text me again. Just not during the game. Hail.

wireTaps: With Terry out, who's our WR1 the rest of the way: Antonio Williams or Treylon Burks?
